market_question: Will US withdraw from NATO before 2027?
reasoning: The US Congress enacted a law in 2020 requiring Senate consent or an act of Congress to withdraw from NATO, sharply raising the domestic political hurdle. Even if a president attempted to unilaterally send a denunciation notice, strong bipartisan opposition and likely legal challenges would deter such an extreme step; Trump’s first-term NATO threats were never executed, and his reelection probability is far from certain. I estimate the true chance of formal notice by end-2026 is only about 2.5%, far below the market’s implied ~7.8%.
evidence_points: FY2020 NDAA (Sec. 1247) prohibits US withdrawal from NATO without Senate two‑thirds vote or an act of Congress.
Trump did not initiate NATO withdrawal during his first term despite frequent threats; core Republican senators such as Graham and McConnell have publicly opposed withdrawal.
All plausible 2024 winners maintain NATO commitments; even a Trump return faces united institutional and legal opposition.
sources_consulted: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (S.1790, Sec. 1247)
Council on Foreign Relations backgrounder on NATO withdrawal
Historical reporting on Trump’s NATO statements and outcomes
